statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail edges up to 22% because NQ futures broke the overnight range and printed a new low at 28,954.50 while the US 10-year yield extended to 4.82%, but easing crude and a contained VIX leave the amplifiers unaligned, so Tail stays below the block threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 12:00-15:00 UTC danger window covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with a second single-hour checkpoint at the 21:00 UTC Broadcom call. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures print a fresh overnight low near 28,955 as the US 10-year yield extends to 4.82%, while Brent eases toward its day low and VIX stays contained
body:
The change this hour is a genuine break of the overnight range. NQ futures trade at 28,986.75 on one quote and 28,983.50 on a second independent quote, about -0.48% against the 29,125.50 previous close, after printing a new session low at 28,954.50. That low takes out the 29,016.50 floor which had held since the Asian session and was still intact at the previous assessment, and it puts futures below the 29,077.22 Nasdaq-100 cash close from Sep 1. Price is currently around 30 points above the new low, in the lower quarter of a 28,954.50-29,170.00 range.

The driver is the long end rather than energy. The US 10-year yield is 4.82%, up about 2 basis points on the day and a fresh high above the 4.800% intraday peak set on Sep 1, while the 2-year is roughly unchanged at 4.41%. That is a bear steepening, consistent with a term-premium and inflation-expectations move rather than a repricing of the near-term policy path, and it is the same channel that has pressured index valuation since the Sep 1 open. Fed funds futures continue to price around a 70% probability of an increase at the September 16 FOMC meeting.

What keeps this from reading as a pathological price path is the absence of aligned amplifiers. Brent is $94.90 against a $94.55-$97.01 day range, so crude sits near the low end of its range and is de-escalating rather than extending after the Sep 1 surge on US strikes against IRGC targets and the attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz. VIX is 16.61 inside a narrow 16.34-16.79 range, up only 1.65%, which is a contained reading to accompany a new index low. A break of a low with easing crude, a flat 2-year and a quiet volatility index is a rates-led drift, not the multi-amplifier alignment that would justify treating mean reversion as failing.

Tail is therefore raised only modestly, from 20% to 22%, and the dominant mode is set to trend-down to reflect the sequential lower lows through the European morning rather than the two-way whipsaw of the preceding hours. Stress rises from 71% to 73% because the backdrop of a fresh cycle high in the long end, an unresolved Middle East escalation and a live September hike debate remains a difficult environment. Confidence is 87%, one point below the previous cycle: two independent futures quotes, VIX, Brent, live 10-year and 2-year yields and the verified event calendar were all obtained this cycle, but the shared Finviz cross-asset context is more than four hours old and was therefore treated as stale and excluded from breadth, megacap and semiconductor confirmation.

The declared danger window is unchanged at 12:00-15:00 UTC, covering the ADP release at 12:15 UTC, the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA crude inventory prints at 14:00 and 14:30 UTC. That cluster is where a rates-led drift could become an opening-auction continuation, and where an EIA surprise could restart the energy leg into a live Hormuz supply premium. A second single-hour checkpoint sits at 21:00 UTC, when Broadcom reports Q3 FY2026 after the close and holds its call, a top-weight semiconductor constituent moving in thin post-close futures. Everything beyond the current hour is conditional risk rather than observed structure.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours open at the peak of the Sep 1 stress episode: Tail sat at 26% at 09:00 UTC and climbed to 31% by 13:00 UTC as the US-Iran escalation, the roughly 6% crude surge and the global long-end selloff were priced in around the Sep 1 US cash open, with Stress reaching 75%. From 14:00 UTC the regime shifted to event/whipsaw and Tail decayed into a 20-25% band, briefly returning to 25% at 19:00 UTC when a new US strike wave broke the cash session low inside the closing hour before that break was reclaimed. Through the overnight and Asian hours Tail held a narrow 20-23% range while Stress stayed persistently high at 71-77%, describing a difficult, high-volatility environment in which retracements kept occurring rather than a sustained one-way trend. The most recent published hour was the calmest of the sequence at Tail 20% and Stress 71%. Three hourly slots - 15:00 and 20:00 UTC on Sep 1 and 01:00 UTC on Sep 2 - have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable with null fields.
outlookSummary: The projection holds Tail in a 21-22% band through the European morning, then lifts it above the block threshold only for the three-hour catalyst cluster from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, with the single highest reading of 27% in the 13:00 UTC hour containing the US opening auction. That is the declared danger window, and the named conditions for it are an ADP upside surprise reinforcing the 4.82% long-end move, opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks, and an EIA inventory surprise restarting the energy leg. One further hour reaches the threshold at 21:00 UTC around the Broadcom results and call. Tail then decays through the US afternoon and the Asian handover to an overnight floor of 17%, and lifts modestly into the Sep 3 European session ahead of a calendar carrying Jobless Claims, Balance of Trade and a Waller speech at 12:30 UTC and ISM Services at 14:00 UTC. Stress stays elevated to high throughout because the crude, sovereign-yield and Fed-repricing backdrop is structural rather than intraday, easing only gradually overnight. Confidence decays from 87% to 50% across the horizon because no live price-path evidence exists for the later windows at the assessment cutoff. Every reading after the current hour is conditional risk, not observed structure.
